title.value: Finding the needle in a high-dimensional haystack: Canonical correlation analysis for neuroscientists
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Finding the needle in a high-dimensional haystack: Canonical correlation analysis for neuroscientists

analysis.description: The paper presents Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) as a method to explore complex multivariate links in neuroscience datasets. It provides insights into CCA's applicability by detailing its modeling principles and scientific applications to bridge variable datasets, such as brain and behavioral data. The paper also discusses different applications of CCA in neuroscience and provides practical guidelines for its implementation.

type.justification: The paper discusses the methodologies and mathematical foundations of Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA), providing insights into how CCA can be applied rather than directly conducting experiments.
type.quote: Our conceptual primer describes how CCA can deepen understanding of large multi-variable datasets in fields such as cognitive neuroscience.

name.justification: The paper focusses on bridging relationships between datasets in neuroscience, especially through brain imaging data and phenotypic behavioral data.
name.quote: The complexity of such “big data” repositories offer new opportunities and pose new challenges for systems neuroscience.

name.justification: The paper discusses using machine learning techniques, particularly Canonical Correlation Analysis, to analyze multivariate datasets.
The paper deals with large biomedical datasets, such as those in neuroscience and behavioral studies.
name.quote: similar to the advent of microarrays in genetics, brain-imaging and extensive behavioral phenotyping yield datasets with tens of thousands of variables.

name.justification: CCA is the central model discussed throughout the paper for analyzing complex multivariate data in neuroscience.
name.quote: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is a prototypical family of methods that is useful in identifying the links between variable sets from different modalities.

is_contributed.justification: CCA is explained and applied in the paper as a pre-existing method, not introduced for the first time.
is_contributed.quote: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is a multivariate statistical method that was introduced in the 1930s (Hotelling, 1936).

is_executed.justification: The paper is more theoretical, describing applications of CCA beyond practical execution or computational implementation.
is_executed.quote: These considerations illustrate why CCA applications have long been less attractive in the context of many neuroscience studies, while its appeal and feasibility are now steadily growing as ever more rich, multi-modal, and open datasets become available (Davis et al., 2014).

is_compared.justification: CCA is compared with other multivariate methods throughout the paper, such as PCA and ICA.
is_compared.quote: CCA instead directly optimizes the correspondence between the latent dimensions directly in the embedding space, rather than the reconstruction loss in the original variables incurred by the low-rank bottleneck.

referenced_paper_title.quote: Canonical correlation analysis (Hotelling, 1936) determines the relationship between variable sets from two domains of measurement.
